info.title: Western Astrology API
info.description:
Western astrology API for natal birth charts with an editorial reading of the whole chart, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly horoscopes with unique content per sign and the dated sky events behind every reading, synastry compatibility scores, composite charts, solar and lunar returns, real-time transit aspects, and moon phases. 4 house systems (Placidus, Koch, Whole Sign, Equal) with accurate tropical ephemeris, aspect-pattern detection (Grand Trine, T-Square, Yod), astrocartography planetary lines, relocation charts, and local space maps for location based astrology, plus classical and professional points like fixed star conjunctions, Arabic lots, the asteroid goddesses (Ceres, Pallas, Juno, Vesta), mean and true Black Moon Lilith, and timing techniques like secondary progressions, solar arc directions, and annual profections. Built for horoscope platforms, astrology dating apps, AI chatbots, wellness products, and zodiac content engines. Schedule future horoscopes by date or by year for editorial workflows, no astronomy expertise needed. One key covers every RoxyAPI domain, with Remote MCP and typed SDKs.

# RoxyAPI: the Spiritual OS layer for agentic AI

> **Base URL:** `https://roxyapi.com/api/v2`. Every path below is relative to it.

One API key for 18+ insight domains (Western Astrology, Vedic Astrology, Forecast, Human Design, Chinese Astrology, Feng Shui, Mesoamerican Astrology, Vastu Shastra, Numerology, Kabbalah, Tarot Reading, Biorhythm, Ayurveda, I-Ching Oracle, Crystals and Healing Stones, Dream Interpretation, Angel Numbers, Location and Timezone), 261+ endpoints, planetary positions read directly from the NASA JPL DE440 ephemeris and verified against NASA JPL Horizons, and every calculation held by 3,683 gold standard tests. Readings come back as structured data with editorial interpretation text, translated into 10+ languages via `?lang=` on translated endpoints. Remote MCP servers, typed SDKs for TypeScript, Python, PHP, C#, Go, Rust, and Dart, drop-in UI components and copy-paste widgets, and open source Templates all run on this one document.

## Who builds on RoxyAPI

- **Developers** shipping astrology, tarot, numerology and wellness apps without learning each system first
- **AI agent builders** giving Claude, GPT or Gemini real calculations instead of guesses, over Remote MCP
- **Vibe coders** building with Cursor, Claude Code, Bolt or Replit from the spec and AGENTS.md
- **Founders and brands** launching insight products for their audience on one key

## Quick start

**1. Get a key** at [roxyapi.com/pricing](https://roxyapi.com/pricing). It is ready the moment payment clears.

**2. Make your first call:**
```bash
curl -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" https://roxyapi.com/api/v2/astrology/horoscope/aries/daily
```

**3. Check your usage:**
```bash
curl -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY" https://roxyapi.com/api/v2/usage
```

## AI agents: Remote MCP

Every domain has its own Remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP at `https://roxyapi.com/mcp/{domain}` (for example `/mcp/astrology`), 258+ tools in all, with nothing to install or host. Add the URL to Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT or any MCP client, or connect from the OpenAI Agents SDK and Gemini ADK. Coding agents that build against this API use the documentation server at `/mcp/docs`. Setup for every client: [roxyapi.com/docs/mcp](https://roxyapi.com/docs/mcp).

## Authentication

Send your key as `X-API-Key: YOUR_KEY` (recommended), as `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY`, or as the `?api_key=` query parameter for quick tests. Keep secret keys on a server; publishable keys are for the browser.

## Responses and limits

Clean JSON with no wrapper. An error returns `{ "error", "code", "doc_url" }`: `error` is readable and may change wording, `code` is stable and the one to switch on, and `doc_url` links to the fix for that exact code.

Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Used` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` for your monthly allowance, which resets on the 1st of each month at 00:00 UTC. Each plan also has a per-minute limit for bursts, from 600 requests per minute on Starter; going over it answers `429` with a `Retry-After` and never counts against the month.

## Errors

Every code the API returns, also published machine-readably as `x-error-codes` on the `info` object of this document:

| Status | Code | When |
|--------|------|------|
| 400 | [`validation_error`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#validation_error) | A field is missing or invalid. The body lists every failing field at once in issues, each with its path and the expected shape. |
| 400 | [`bad_request`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#bad_request) | The request was rejected as a whole, for example a body that is not valid JSON or a date range that ends before it starts. |
| 400 | [`date_out_of_range`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#date_out_of_range) | A date lies outside the span the planetary positions are served for. The error names the supported dates. |
| 400 | [`invalid_branding`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#invalid_branding) | The report branding cannot be used, for example a logo that is not a PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG image. |
| 400 | [`logo_fetch_failed`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#logo_fetch_failed) | The report logo could not be fetched: it must be an HTTPS URL on a public host that answers within the size limit. |
| 400 | [`unsupported_character`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#unsupported_character) | The report text holds a character no report font draws. The error names it: remove or replace it. |
| 401 | [`api_key_required`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#api_key_required) | No API key was sent. |
| 401 | [`invalid_api_key`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#invalid_api_key) | The key sent is malformed or cannot be verified. |
| 401 | [`api_key_revoked`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#api_key_revoked) | The key was valid once and has since been revoked from the account page. |
| 401 | [`subscription_not_found`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#subscription_not_found) | The key verifies, but the subscription behind it no longer exists. |
| 401 | [`subscription_inactive`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#subscription_inactive) | The subscription behind the key is cancelled, expired or suspended, or a trial is past its end date. |
| 401 | [`publishable_key_not_allowed_on_mcp`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#publishable_key_not_allowed_on_mcp) | A publishable key was used on a Remote MCP server, which takes a secret key. |
| 401 | [`invalid_client_ip`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#invalid_client_ip) | A keyless request could not be attributed to a caller. |
| 401 | [`unauthorized`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#unauthorized) | Authentication failed with no more specific reason to give. |
| 403 | [`forbidden`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#forbidden) | The key is valid, but this request is not permitted. |
| 403 | [`origin_required`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#origin_required) | A publishable key with an origin allowlist was used with no Origin header, as from a server or a native app. |
| 403 | [`origin_not_allowed`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#origin_not_allowed) | The calling site is not on the origin allowlist of this publishable key. |
| 404 | [`not_found`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#not_found) | Nothing is served at this path, or the identifier in it does not exist. A path miss adds suggestions, the closest real endpoints. |
| 405 | [`method_not_allowed`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#method_not_allowed) | The path exists for a different HTTP method. The body lists the accepted methods in allow, as does the Allow header. |
| 409 | [`conflict`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#conflict) | The request cannot be applied in the current state. |
| 410 | [`gone`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#gone) | The path was removed permanently. |
| 413 | [`payload_too_large`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#payload_too_large) | The request body is larger than the API accepts. A body far over the cap is refused before it reaches the API and returns a bare 413 with no JSON body. |
| 415 | [`unsupported_media_type`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#unsupported_media_type) | A request with a body was sent without Content-Type: application/json. |
| 422 | [`unprocessable_entity`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#unprocessable_entity) | Every field is valid, but the combination cannot be computed. |
| 429 | [`rate_limit_exceeded`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#rate_limit_exceeded) | The monthly request allowance is used up. Retry-After gives the seconds to the reset. |
| 429 | [`rate_limit_per_minute`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#rate_limit_per_minute) | The per-minute limit of the plan was reached. Retry-After gives the seconds to the next minute, and the monthly allowance is not charged. |
| 429 | [`rate_limited`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#rate_limited) | A rate limit was reached, reported without the plan detail. |
| 429 | [`free_tier_exhausted`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#free_tier_exhausted) | A keyless request has used up its trial allowance. |
| 429 | [`reports_rate_limited`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#reports_rate_limited) | Too many reports were requested this minute. Retry-After gives the seconds to the next minute. |
| 500 | [`internal_error`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#internal_error) | The request failed inside our service. Retry with exponential backoff. |
| 503 | [`compute_saturated`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#compute_saturated) | Heavy calculations are briefly at capacity. Send the same request again after Retry-After seconds. |
| 503 | [`reports_busy`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#reports_busy) | Report rendering is briefly at capacity. Send the same request again after Retry-After seconds. |
| 503 | [`report_render_timeout`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#report_render_timeout) | The report took too long to render. Send the same request again. |
| Any | [`error`](https://roxyapi.com/docs/errors#error) | A fallback for a status with no more specific code. The status and the error field carry the signal. |

## Pricing

One flat subscription covers every domain, every endpoint, Remote MCP, the SDKs, UI components, widgets and every language. Every data endpoint is one request, a planet position or a full birth chart, with no credits and no per-product fees. From $39 per month for 50K requests, up to 3M requests, with custom volume above that: [roxyapi.com/pricing](https://roxyapi.com/pricing).

## Resources

- [Quickstart](https://roxyapi.com/docs/quickstart): the first call in three steps
- [Documentation](https://roxyapi.com/docs): guides, tutorials and a reference per domain
- [Remote MCP](https://roxyapi.com/docs/mcp): connect an AI agent
- [SDKs](https://roxyapi.com/docs/sdk) and [UI components](https://roxyapi.com/ui)
- [Templates](https://roxyapi.com/templates): open source apps to clone and deploy
- [Methodology](https://roxyapi.com/methodology): how accuracy is verified
- [Contact](https://roxyapi.com/contact): support and key recovery

apiKey.name: X-API-Key
apiKey.description: Your API key for accessing RoxyAPI. Alternatively, you can pass the API key as a query parameter "api_key".

opening.description: Whole-chart natal reading connecting the Sun, Moon, Ascendant, central signature and the tension that shapes their expression.
opening.example:
What you chase and what calms you rarely agree on timing, so the urge to shelter loved ones keeps tripping over a need for quick release. Your Scorpio rising fits your Sun like a well-cut coat, comfortable from the first wearing and roomy enough to move in without a second thought.

If one bond defines you, it is the Sun tied to Jupiter, near enough that their dealings play out in everything you do. There is nothing hidden about what steers you, since Pluto rules Scorpio rising while occupying a commanding place in Scorpio, drawing you again and again toward your sense of self and first impressions. Real results settle you more than promises do, so you see jobs through, tidy as you go, and believe the evidence of a spirit level or a measuring tape. Initiative comes as standard: you spot the gap nobody has filled yet and step into it before the meeting even ends.

Your aims and your comfort seldom keep the same schedule, and a drive to give people a home and a quick outlet for strong feelings keep cutting in on one another, so plenty of what you build is built to end the dispute. The friction settles once it has a job, and a project, a deadline or a craft gives the two sides somewhere to meet instead of somewhere to collide. Much of the strain eases through Venus, since it gives the Moon a clear outlet and a little more room.

love.description: Relationships chapter connecting the seventh-house ruler and occupants with the Venus-Mars relationship.
love.example: Whom you let near, and how you keep the balance once they arrive, shapes much of your growth and many of your best surprises. You look for people who show care through presence and comfort, and a long bond rewards consistency over excitement, held loosely enough never to cling. Venus, guiding your close ties, lies in the eighth house of depth and trust, so you want bonds that go all the way down, and you test them before you settle in. Words are a playground: Neptune, which oversees your fifth house, lives in your third, so clever messages, word games, short trips and lively chats with neighbors bring out your playful side.

career.description: Career chapter connecting the tenth-house ruler and occupants with the Midheaven sign.
career.example: Whatever you call your work, you want it to leave a mark, a contribution others recognize and a reputation you would gladly sign. Purpose counts for more than rank: placed in your ninth house of beliefs and higher learning, the Sun draws you to work built around an idea you can defend. A Leo Midheaven steers you toward visible, creative leadership, output that carries your signature and brightens any room it reaches.

home.description: Home chapter connecting the fourth-house ruler and occupants with the IC sign and private foundations.
home.example: You carry where you come from into wherever you live now, keeping the patterns that serve you and building fresh shelter around them. Feeling settled and feeling resourced are close cousins for you: Uranus, overseer of your fourth house, lives in your second, among possessions and self-esteem. With Aquarius among your roots, you feel most at home among like minds, and freedom outranks tradition for you.

closing.description: Closing synthesis returning to the central drives, their integration and the chart signature.
closing.example: Most of what you take on becomes a truce, with a fiercely protective streak getting its way and the freedom to feel at full heat kept content. Turn to Venus when the strain builds, because its easy link to the Moon makes that part of you easier to live with. Worked with, the restlessness becomes a knack for finishing, so you are frequently halfway down the road before other people have settled whether to start. You keep your deepest truths close and spend them only where they count.

interpretation.description: Whole-chart natal interpretation. Present when lang is one the natal engine writes (English, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish); absent otherwise.

date.description: Birth date used for this chart (YYYY-MM-DD).

time.description: Birth time used for this chart (HH:MM:SS, 24-hour).

latitude.description: Birth latitude in decimal degrees.

longitude.description: Birth longitude in decimal degrees.

timezone.description: Timezone offset from UTC in decimal hours.

birthDetails.description: Birth details echoed back from the request. Confirms the input used for this chart calculation.

name.description: Planet or point name (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, North Node, South Node, Chiron, Black Moon Lilith). Always English, whatever the lang parameter says, so it stays safe to compare against in code. Use nameLocalized for anything a reader sees. The lunar nodes follow the request nodeType, which defaults to the true (osculating) node; pass "mean" for the smoothed node. The two differ by up to about 1.8 degrees and no other body is affected. Black Moon Lilith is always the mean lunar apogee, whatever nodeType says. POST /lilith returns the mean and the true (osculating) apogee side by side, each labelled by its variant.

nameLocalized.description: Planet or point name in the requested language, for display only. Present only when lang is set to a language other than English, since in English it would repeat its canonical partner field exactly. Never compare against this value, compare against the canonical field beside it.

longitude.description: Apparent geocentric tropical longitude on the true ecliptic of date, in degrees (0-360): light time and aberration applied, nutation included, the convention desktop chart software and the NASA JPL Horizons observer tables print, so it compares directly with either.

latitude.description: Apparent geocentric ecliptic latitude of date, in degrees.

sign.description: Tropical zodiac sign this planet occupies. Always English, whatever the lang parameter says, so it stays safe to compare against in code. Use signLocalized for anything a reader sees.

signLocalized.description: Zodiac sign name in the requested language, for display only. Present only when lang is set to a language other than English, since in English it would repeat its canonical partner field exactly. Never compare against this value, compare against the canonical field beside it.

house.description: House placement (1-12) based on the selected house system.

speed.description: Daily motion in degrees per day. Negative values indicate retrograde.

isRetrograde.description: Whether the planet is in retrograde motion.

dignity.description: Essential dignity of this body in the sign it occupies: domicile (the sign it rules, its strongest placement), exaltation (honoured and amplified), detriment (opposite its rulership, where it struggles), fall (opposite its exaltation, where it is weakened), or peregrine (in none of its own dignity signs). Absent for the lunar nodes, Chiron and Black Moon Lilith, which rule no sign and therefore hold no dignity at all, so an absent field and peregrine are different answers. Derived by sign only, so triplicity, bounds and face are not considered. Always English, whatever the lang parameter says, so it stays safe to compare against in code. The four dignity signs behind it are published per body by GET /planet-meanings/{id}.

summary.description: The placement in brief: what this body does in its sign and in its house, written for this chart.
summary.example: Belonging is the root of your power, and you are most yourself with your people gathered close. Faith, scholarship and far shores stretch you, and every wider view adds to who you are becoming.

detailed.description: The full reading of this placement: its sign and house, and where they apply its dignity, retrograde motion, the Moon phase at birth, a nearby angle and its tightest aspect.
detailed.example: You remember birthdays, keep every handwritten note, and notice who stopped talking halfway through dinner. Your instincts catch a mood before anyone names it, and they are seldom wrong about who needs care. When exposed, you pull into your shell and wait to be guessed, though putting words to the need works faster. Home is wherever you set down your care, and even a rented room soon starts to feel lived in. A map, a syllabus or a heated debate about what life is for wakes you up. You shine as a seeker who loves explaining what you found to anyone curious enough to ask. A single trip abroad can change how you see everything back home for years. Optimism sits near the core with Jupiter beside the Sun, so big ideas get an easy welcome and the details are trusted to sort themselves out.

longitude.description: Ecliptic longitude of this house cusp (0-360).

Present only when lang is set to a language other than English, since in English it would repeat its canonical partner field exactly. houseSystem.description: House system used for this chart (placidus, whole-sign, equal, or koch).

planet1Localized.description: First planet name in the requested language, for display only. planet2Localized.description: Second planet name in the requested language, for display only. Present only when lang is set to a language other than English, since in English it would repeat its canonical partner field exactly. typeLocalized.description: Aspect type name in the requested language, for display only. Present only when lang is set to a language other than English, since in English it would repeat its canonical partner field exactly. Never compare against this value, compare against the canonical field beside it.

angle.description: Exact angle of this aspect type in degrees.

orb.description: Distance from exact aspect in degrees. Tighter orb means stronger influence.

isApplying.description: Whether the aspect is applying (growing stronger) or separating (fading).

strength.description: Aspect strength percentage (0-100) based on orb tightness.

interpretation.example: harmonious
interpretation.description: Aspect nature: harmonious, challenging, or neutral. Always English, whatever the lang parameter says, because it is an identifier to compare and style on. Read aspectInterpretation for the sentence a reader sees.

summary.example: Your North Node in Aquarius points toward less familiar ground, while the South Node in Leo marks what you already know by heart.
summary.description: Short read of THIS pair of bodies as the aspect joins them in this chart. Type, orb, strength and motion stay in the fields beside it. Translated in place, so it arrives in the requested language.

keywords.description: Themes this aspect activates between the two bodies. Translated in place, so they arrive in the requested language.

aspectInterpretation.description: Narrative interpretation of this aspect for this chart. The reference description of the aspect TYPE is not repeated per row, use GET or POST /astrology/aspects for that card.

aspects.description: All planetary aspects found in this chart with orbs, strength, and interpretation.

kind.description: Pattern kind identifier. GRAND_TRINE (3 trines, harmonious flow), KITE (Grand Trine with a focal outlet planet), T_SQUARE (opposition with squared apex, growth engine), GRAND_CROSS (4 planets in 2 oppositions and 4 squares, peak tension), YOD (a planet at the apex of two quincunxes, a call to adjust), MYSTIC_RECTANGLE (oppositions softened by trines and sextiles), STELLIUM (3+ planets clustered in a sign or 10-degree arc).

name.description: Human-readable name of the configuration as used in astrological literature.

planets.description: Participating bodies in canonical order. For Kite, T-Square, and Yod the apex planet appears first.

apex.description: Focal planet for Kite, T-Square, and Yod patterns. Receives the released energy of the configuration and is the recommended integration point.

element.description: Dominant element when the pattern is element-coherent (Grand Trine, Kite). Reported lowercase. Absent for patterns whose meaning does not pivot on element.

modality.description: Dominant modality for tension-based patterns (T-Square, Grand Cross). Cardinal initiates, Fixed sustains, Mutable adapts.

dissociate.description: True if the pattern is out-of-sign (one or more planets in a neighboring element or modality). Dissociate patterns are still valid but operate with weakened thematic coherence.

tightness.description: Tightness score (0-100) derived from the average orb tightness across all defining aspects. Higher means closer to exact and stronger thematic expression.

interpretation.example: Your Sun, Moon, and Mars form a Grand Trine, an easy triangle of support, so talent passes between them without effort and grows most when you put it to deliberate use.
interpretation.description: Concise one-line interpretation naming the participating planets and theme. Localized to the requested language via the lang query parameter (defaults to English).

interpretationKey.description: Stable template identifier used to render the interpretation. Useful for clients that wish to swap in a custom narrative template while preserving the structured variables.

additionalProperties.description: One value interpolated into the interpretation template, keyed by the placeholder name it fills. Which keys are present depends on the pattern: a Grand Trine carries an element plus three planets, a T-Square carries an apex.

interpretationVars.description: Variables that were interpolated into the interpretation template. Names already resolved to the requested language where appropriate.

patterns.description: Detected multi-planet aspect configurations (Grand Trine, Kite, T-Square, Grand Cross, Yod, Mystic Rectangle, Stellium). Grand Cross suppresses contained T-Squares, Kite suppresses underlying Grand Trine.

summary.description: Narrative summary of the overall aspect pattern in this chart.
summary.example: Friction drives this chart, which tends to make you someone who grows by working things through rather than waiting for them to settle.

dominant.description: Which way this chart leans, read from the harmonious and challenging counts beside it against how many of each a typical chart holds: harmonious, challenging or balanced. Always English, whatever the lang parameter says; the summary states the same lean in the requested language.

challenging.description: Count of challenging aspects (square, opposition, quincunx).

aspectsInterpretation.description: Aspect pattern analysis showing the balance of harmonious vs challenging energies in the chart.

sign.description: Zodiac sign on the Ascendant (rising sign). Always English, whatever the lang parameter says. Use signLocalized for anything a reader sees.

signLocalized.description: Ascendant sign name in the requested language, for display only. Present only when lang is set to a language other than English, since in English it would repeat its canonical partner field exactly. Never compare against this value, compare against the canonical field beside it.

longitude.description: Absolute ecliptic longitude of the Ascendant (0-360).

summary.example: Intensity is your handshake, a steady gaze and a few chosen words that leave people wanting to know what you are thinking.
summary.description: One-sentence read of the rising sign: how you meet the world and how others first meet you.

detailed.example: Someone tells you a light story and you hear the heavier one underneath it, which is why your silence makes some people say more than they planned. First meetings with you feel charged, as though more is being said under the words, and newcomers either lean closer or take a careful step back. Anything new gets investigated beneath the surface first, and you prefer knowing the hidden costs and motives before you commit a single ounce of trust. Privacy hardens into secrecy under scrutiny, and control or a stinging remark becomes the defense, while sharing one true thing first eases the standoff for everyone. Most people sense deep water in you, calm on top and strong underneath, and the few who swim farther find a fiercely devoted ally.

detailed.example: You keep at a creative goal long after others drift, rehearsing, revising and polishing, because you want the finished piece to carry your name with real pride. Others read you as magnetic and commanding, someone whose confidence warms a room rather than chilling it, and people gravitate toward you without being asked. Persistence matters to you as much as flair, and the achievement you prize is a creative effort sustained over years, not one bright evening. Applause can begin to seem like oxygen, and the steadier fuel is the satisfaction of watching someone you encouraged step forward and shine on their own. Warmth and boldness travel together wherever you show up publicly, and people tend to remember the glow of working near you more than any single result.

nodeType.description: Lunar node convention. "mean" is the smoothed average node, which always moves retrograde; "true" is the osculating node, which tracks the real perturbed node, oscillates up to about 1.5 degrees either side of the mean on a 173-day cycle, and can briefly turn direct. Neither is more correct and they almost always fall in the same sign. Applies to the North and South Node. True is the osculating node and the default, because it is what most Western chart software reports; mean is the smoothed node preferred by several evolutionary schools, so pass "mean" to match one. Nothing else in the chart changes, and the two agree on the sign except when the node sits within about 1.8 degrees of a cusp. Defaults to "true".

houseSystem.description: House system for dividing the chart into 12 houses. Placidus (default) is most popular in Western astrology and time-sensitive. post.summary: Get planetary positions - Ephemeris calculator for all planets
post.description: Calculate accurate tropical zodiac positions for all 14 celestial bodies for any date, time, and location. The bodies are the 10 classical planets Sun through Pluto, the lunar nodes, Chiron, and Black Moon Lilith. Returns longitude, latitude, zodiac sign, degree within sign, daily motion speed, retrograde status, and a reading of each body in its sign. Perfect for transit tracking, ephemeris tables, astrology apps, and planetary position widgets. Verified against NASA JPL Horizons.

schema.description: Response language (BCP 47). Supported: en, tr, de, es, hi, pt, fr, ru, zh-Hans, zh-Hant. Defaults to en. Coverage varies by domain, and a field with no translation in the requested language returns English.

parameters.name: lang

date.description: Target date for planetary positions in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use current date for transit positions, or any historical/future date for research. Planets move daily, so this date determines their zodiac positions.

time.description: Time in 24-hour HH:MM:SS format for precise calculations. Moon moves ~13° per day, so time matters for accurate lunar position. Use 12:00:00 (noon) as default if exact time not needed.

nodeType.description: Lunar node convention. "mean" is the smoothed average node, which always moves retrograde; "true" is the osculating node, which tracks the real perturbed node, oscillates up to about 1.5 degrees either side of the mean on a 173-day cycle, and can briefly turn direct. Neither is more correct and they almost always fall in the same sign. Applies to the North and South Node. True is the osculating node and the default, because it is what most Western chart software reports; mean is the smoothed node preferred by several evolutionary schools, so pass "mean" to match one. Nothing else in the chart changes, and the two agree on the sign except when the node sits within about 1.8 degrees of a cusp. Defaults to "true".

latitude.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees (-90 to 90). While planetary longitudes are geocentric (same worldwide), this is needed for house calculations if extending functionality. For basic ephemeris, use 0 as default.

longitude.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees (-180 to 180). Used for precise local time conversion. For basic planetary positions, this has minimal impact but ensures accuracy.

timezone.description: Decimal hours from UTC (e.g. -5 for EST, 5.5 for IST, 9 for JST, 5.75 for NPT) OR IANA name (e.g. "America/New_York"). IANA resolved to the DST-correct offset for the chart date.

name.description: Planet name (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, North Node, South Node, Chiron, Black Moon Lilith). The lunar nodes follow the request nodeType, which defaults to the true (osculating) node; pass "mean" for the smoothed node. The two differ by up to about 1.8 degrees and no other body is affected. Black Moon Lilith is always the mean lunar apogee, whatever nodeType says. POST /lilith returns the mean and the true (osculating) apogee side by side, each labelled by its variant.

longitude.description: Apparent geocentric tropical longitude on the true ecliptic of date, in degrees (0-360): light time and aberration applied, nutation included, the convention desktop chart software and the NASA JPL Horizons observer tables print, so it compares directly with either.

post.summary: Monthly Aspects - Tropical aspect calendar for an entire month
post.description: Get every planetary aspect that perfects during a given month, across the 13 non-lunar Western bodies: the Sun and Mercury through Pluto, both lunar nodes, Chiron and Black Moon Lilith. Detects nine aspects, five major (conjunction, sextile, square, trine, opposition) and four minor (semi-sextile, semi-square, sesquiquadrate, quincunx), each with its own traditional orb, and returns the exact date and time of closest approach in your timezone along with the nature of the aspect. post.summary: Monthly Parallels - Declination contacts for an entire month
post.description: Get every parallel and contraparallel of declination that perfects during a given month, across the 13 non-lunar Western bodies: the Sun and Mercury through Pluto, both lunar nodes, Chiron and Black Moon Lilith. A parallel is two bodies at the same declination and reads much like a conjunction; a contraparallel is equal and opposite declinations and reads much like an opposition. Neither depends on zodiacal distance, so they surface connections an aspect table cannot show, which is why traditional and modern practitioners read them alongside aspects. Declinations are geocentric, matching what an ephemeris publishes. Returns the exact date and time of closest approach in your timezone with both declinations. The Moon is excluded because its declination swings the full range every month and would bury the slow pairs. Omit year and month to get the month in progress, so a published calendar stays current without a redeploy. Essential for declination work, out-of-bounds tracking, monthly forecast copy, and electional timing. Monthly parallel calendar API, declination aspects, contraparallel ephemeris. Verified against NASA JPL Horizons.

"mean" is the smoothed average node, which always moves retrograde; "true" is the osculating node, which tracks the real perturbed node, oscillates up to about 1.5 degrees either side of the mean on a 173-day cycle, and can briefly turn direct. Neither is more correct and they almost always fall in the same sign. Applies to the North and South Node. True is the osculating node and the default, because it is what most Western chart software reports; mean is the smoothed node preferred by several evolutionary schools, so pass "mean" to match one. Nothing else in the chart changes, and the two agree on the sign except when the node sits within about 1.8 degrees of a cusp. Defaults to "true".

post.description: Get every moment a body crosses the plane of the ecliptic during a given year, for the 11 Western bodies that leave it: the Moon and Mercury through Pluto, plus Chiron and Black Moon Lilith. A crossing from south to north is an ascending node passage, north to south a descending one. These are the instants a body sits exactly on the ecliptic rather than merely near it, which is what makes an eclipse possible when a lunar crossing coincides with a New or Full Moon, and what practitioners use for node-based timing. Returns the exact date and time in your timezone with the tropical longitude and sign. The Sun and the lunar nodes are excluded because they lie on the plane by definition and so have no nodes of their own. Essential for eclipse-season work, node timing, and astronomical calendars. Ecliptic crossing API, planetary node passage, ascending and descending nodes. Verified against NASA JPL Horizons.

The composite chart represents the relationship as a single entity, showing its core identity, emotional bond, communication style, and growth direction. Composite chart API, midpoint chart calculator, relationship astrology, couple chart analysis.

get.summary: Daily horoscope by zodiac sign - Transit-based editorial columns
get.description: A publish-ready column for any zodiac sign, built from the dated transits over it. Each response returns those events and the standing position of every planet, so every date and claim can be fact-checked. The reading names the aspects, sign ingresses, lunations and retrograde stations driving it and reads each into the whole-sign houses of that sign, so every sign gets different content rather than one blurb reused twelve times. Alongside the column come overview, love, career, health, finance and advice, the active transits, Moon sign and phase, an energy rating, lucky number and color, and compatible signs. No language model is involved, so a given sign and date always returns the same text and a piece scheduled months ahead is the piece that runs. The day is read on a clock you choose, UTC by default, so a transit the evening before in the timezone of the end user is never called today. Pass date for editorial scheduling, or timezone for the local day of the end user. Composed in 8 languages (en, tr, de, es, hi, pt, fr, ru); zh-Hans and zh-Hant read English. Daily horoscope API, zodiac forecast, sun sign horoscope, astrology prediction.

column.description: The full column for this period, ready to run as one piece, its paragraphs, where it has more than one, separated by a blank line. The six section fields each open on an event or standing planet of their own read through their life area, the one named in focus on the lead of this column, so render either shape and never both. Deterministic: the same sign and period always returns the same column.

focus.description: The topic this reading is mainly about: love, career, finance or health when the lead event falls in that life area, overview for a bigger-picture period. A machine value, canonical English in every language, so a client can route its own content on it (a related article, a product, a call to action) without parsing the prose; the topic field it names reads the same lead the column opens on.

type.description: Kind of event. aspect is an exact angle between two moving bodies, sign-ingress a body entering a new sign, retrograde-station a body turning retrograde or direct, lunar-phase one of the four quarters, eclipse a solar or lunar eclipse, and solar-season the Sun entering a sign.

at.description: Exact instant the event perfects, ISO 8601 to the second, on the clock the reading is read on: UTC with Z by default, the offset of timezone when one is passed on a daily, weekly or monthly reading (2026-11-13T19:27:27-05:00 in New York), the same instant either way; a yearly reading is written in UTC. Verifiable against NASA JPL Horizons for a position event and against the US Naval Observatory for a lunar phase or eclipse.

bodies.description: Bodies involved, canonical English regardless of the requested language so the value stays safe to switch on. Two entries for an aspect, faster body first. One entry for an ingress, a station, a lunar phase, or an eclipse.

name.description: Body name, canonical English in every language. Matches the entry at the same index in bodies.

sign.description: Sign this body occupies at the event timestamp, lowercase and never translated. For a sign change, the sign entered.

house.description: Whole-sign house this body occupies at the event instant, counted from the queried sign, 1 to 12.

placements.description: Each participant at the enclosing event timestamp, in bodies order: two entries for an aspect and one for every other event. Names and signs stay canonical English in every language. Each entry carries its own whole-sign house, including the second body of an aspect. Event placements can differ from positions, which reports noon on the first day of the period.

aspect.description: Angle formed, on aspect events only: conjunction, sextile, square, trine, opposition, semi-sextile, quincunx, semi-square, or sesquiquadrate.

phase.description: Exact quarter phase, on lunar-phase events only: new-moon, first-quarter, full-moon, or last-quarter. Canonical English in every language. Use to identify the phase at the event instant.

kind.description: Eclipse classification at peak, on eclipse events only: penumbral, partial, annular, or total. Canonical English in every language. Sun in bodies identifies a solar eclipse and Moon a lunar eclipse.

direction.description: Direction the body turns at the event instant, on retrograde-station events only: retrograde starts backward motion and direct ends it. Canonical English in every language. Present even when the other end of the retrograde span cannot be dated.

sign.description: Sign the event falls in, lowercase, where it has exactly one. Absent for an aspect whose two bodies stand in different signs.

house.description: Whole-sign house the event falls in, counted from the queried sign, 1 to 12. This is what turns one global sky event into a statement about this reader.

through.description: End of the window this event holds open, on the same clock as at, given only where a bounded window is a real fact about it: the orb span of an aspect, the sign span of an ingress or a season, the retrograde span of a station. Absent for a lunar phase or an eclipse, which are instants and not spans.

events.description: The dated astronomical events this reading is built on, earliest first. Every field in every row can be checked against an independent authority, so a column can be fact-checked before it is published. Empty on a period in which nothing exact happens, where the reading falls back to the standing positions instead.

name.description: Body, canonical English regardless of the requested language: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune or Pluto, in that order, one row each. Same key and values as planets[].name on the natal chart.

sign.description: Sign the body stands in at noon on the first day of the period on the reader clock, lowercase like events[].sign, never translated.

house.description: Whole-sign house that sign is for the queried sign, 1 to 12, counted as events[].house is.

isRetrograde.description: Whether the body moves retrograde at that noon. Same key as planets[].isRetrograde on the natal chart; the daily activeTransits prints the same flag as a translated string.

dignity.description: Essential dignity of the body in that sign, the same value planets[].dignity reports on the natal chart: domicile, exaltation, detriment, fall, or peregrine. Always English. A column or card that calls a body at home or exalted is backed by this value.

enteredAt.description: Instant the body entered this sign, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at. Where the entry is also a row of events[] in this response it is that row at, byte for byte. Absent only where the entry lies too far back to date.

leavesAt.description: Instant the body next leaves this sign, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at: the date a column prints in until April 15. Where it is also in events[] (the ingress that ends the stay, or the through of the ingress that began it) it is that string, byte for byte. Absent only where the exit lies too far ahead to date.

turnsDirectAt.description: Instant the body next turns direct, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at, present only while isRetrograde is true: the date a retrograde is dated by in the prose. Where the station is also in events[] it is that row at or through, byte for byte. Absent only where the turn lies too far ahead to date.

positions.description: Where each of the ten bodies stands for this reading, one row per body, so every standing claim in the prose (a body in a house, until a date, retrograde until it turns direct, exalted or at home) can be checked against the response itself. It carries state only: every aspect, lunation, eclipse, ingress or station of the period is a row of events[]. Against events[], it adds the bodies that do nothing exact in the period (events[] names only what happens), the entry and exit of the sign each stands in (events[].through carries an exit only for an ingress inside the period), the instant a retrograde body turns direct, and dignity. Against activeTransits, which the daily prints as translated strings for the seven visible bodies, it adds Uranus, Neptune and Pluto, the lowercase sign and numeric house as values, the retrograde flag as a boolean, and the three instants. Where an instant appears in both keys it is the same string. Never translated.

luckyNumber.description: Lucky number for the day, 1 to 9, from the traditional planetary number correspondence applied to the planet that governs this sign today. Not a random draw and not a function of the date.

luckyColor.description: Lucky color for the day, the color traditionally ruled by the planet that governs this sign today: Sun gold, Moon silver, Mercury light blue, Venus green, Mars red, Jupiter purple, Saturn brown. When Uranus, Neptune or Pluto governs, the next most governing of the seven classical planets gives the color. Translated with the lang parameter.

compatibleSigns.description: Three zodiac signs most in tune with this sign today, best first. Read from the real sky of the period, so the list moves with the transits instead of repeating a fixed table, and every pick can be traced in positions[]. On a quiet sky it settles on the classic element partners. For the fixed sign-to-sign pairing, read compatibleSigns from the signs endpoint.

crystal.description: Crystal of the day for this sign: a stone traditionally linked to this sign and to the planet that governs it today, stepping down to the next governing planet when none is, and to any stone of the sign after that. Rotates by date among equally fitting stones, so the same sign meets a new stone on consecutive days. Use for daily crystal cards beside the horoscope.

Useful for content widgets and visual indicators.

type.description: Kind of event. aspect is an exact angle between two moving bodies, sign-ingress a body entering a new sign, retrograde-station a body turning retrograde or direct, lunar-phase one of the four quarters, eclipse a solar or lunar eclipse, and solar-season the Sun entering a sign.

at.description: Exact instant the event perfects, ISO 8601 to the second, on the clock the reading is read on: UTC with Z by default, the offset of timezone when one is passed on a daily, weekly or monthly reading (2026-11-13T19:27:27-05:00 in New York), the same instant either way; a yearly reading is written in UTC. Verifiable against NASA JPL Horizons for a position event and against the US Naval Observatory for a lunar phase or eclipse.

bodies.description: Bodies involved, canonical English regardless of the requested language so the value stays safe to switch on. Two entries for an aspect, faster body first. One entry for an ingress, a station, a lunar phase, or an eclipse.

name.description: Body name, canonical English in every language. Matches the entry at the same index in bodies.

sign.description: Sign this body occupies at the event timestamp, lowercase and never translated. For a sign change, the sign entered.

house.description: Whole-sign house this body occupies at the event instant, counted from the queried sign, 1 to 12.

placements.description: Each participant at the enclosing event timestamp, in bodies order: two entries for an aspect and one for every other event. Names and signs stay canonical English in every language. Each entry carries its own whole-sign house, including the second body of an aspect. Event placements can differ from positions, which reports noon on the first day of the period.

aspect.description: Angle formed, on aspect events only: conjunction, sextile, square, trine, opposition, semi-sextile, quincunx, semi-square, or sesquiquadrate.

phase.description: Exact quarter phase, on lunar-phase events only: new-moon, first-quarter, full-moon, or last-quarter. Canonical English in every language. Use to identify the phase at the event instant.

kind.description: Eclipse classification at peak, on eclipse events only: penumbral, partial, annular, or total. Canonical English in every language. Sun in bodies identifies a solar eclipse and Moon a lunar eclipse.

direction.description: Direction the body turns at the event instant, on retrograde-station events only: retrograde starts backward motion and direct ends it. Canonical English in every language. Present even when the other end of the retrograde span cannot be dated.

sign.description: Sign the event falls in, lowercase, where it has exactly one. Absent for an aspect whose two bodies stand in different signs.

house.description: Whole-sign house the event falls in, counted from the queried sign, 1 to 12. This is what turns one global sky event into a statement about this reader.

through.description: End of the window this event holds open, on the same clock as at, given only where a bounded window is a real fact about it: the orb span of an aspect, the sign span of an ingress or a season, the retrograde span of a station. Absent for a lunar phase or an eclipse, which are instants and not spans.

events.description: The dated astronomical events this reading is built on, earliest first. Every field in every row can be checked against an independent authority, so a column can be fact-checked before it is published. Empty on a period in which nothing exact happens, where the reading falls back to the standing positions instead.

name.description: Body, canonical English regardless of the requested language: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune or Pluto, in that order, one row each. Same key and values as planets[].name on the natal chart.

sign.description: Sign the body stands in at noon on the first day of the period on the reader clock, lowercase like events[].sign, never translated.

house.description: Whole-sign house that sign is for the queried sign, 1 to 12, counted as events[].house is.

isRetrograde.description: Whether the body moves retrograde at that noon. Same key as planets[].isRetrograde on the natal chart; the daily activeTransits prints the same flag as a translated string.

dignity.description: Essential dignity of the body in that sign, the same value planets[].dignity reports on the natal chart: domicile, exaltation, detriment, fall, or peregrine. Always English. A column or card that calls a body at home or exalted is backed by this value.

enteredAt.description: Instant the body entered this sign, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at. Where the entry is also a row of events[] in this response it is that row at, byte for byte. Absent only where the entry lies too far back to date.

leavesAt.description: Instant the body next leaves this sign, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at: the date a column prints in until April 15. Where it is also in events[] (the ingress that ends the stay, or the through of the ingress that began it) it is that string, byte for byte. Absent only where the exit lies too far ahead to date.

turnsDirectAt.description: Instant the body next turns direct, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at, present only while isRetrograde is true: the date a retrograde is dated by in the prose. Where the station is also in events[] it is that row at or through, byte for byte. Absent only where the turn lies too far ahead to date.

positions.description: Where each of the ten bodies stands for this reading, one row per body, so every standing claim in the prose (a body in a house, until a date, retrograde until it turns direct, exalted or at home) can be checked against the response itself. It carries state only: every aspect, lunation, eclipse, ingress or station of the period is a row of events[]. Against events[], it adds the bodies that do nothing exact in the period (events[] names only what happens), the entry and exit of the sign each stands in (events[].through carries an exit only for an ingress inside the period), the instant a retrograde body turns direct, and dignity. Against activeTransits, which the daily prints as translated strings for the seven visible bodies, it adds Uranus, Neptune and Pluto, the lowercase sign and numeric house as values, the retrograde flag as a boolean, and the three instants. Where an instant appears in both keys it is the same string. Never translated.

luckyDays.description: The three most favorable days this week, from the planetary rulers of the seven weekdays, ranked by how strongly each of those planets stands for this sign.

luckyNumbers.description: Three lucky numbers for the week, each 1 to 9 and all distinct, from the traditional planetary number correspondence applied to the three planets that govern this sign this week.

compatibleSigns.description: Three zodiac signs most in tune with this sign this week, best first. Read from the real sky of the period, so the list moves with the transits instead of repeating a fixed table, and every pick can be traced in positions[]. On a quiet sky it settles on the classic element partners. For the fixed sign-to-sign pairing, read compatibleSigns from the signs endpoint.

In your identity realm, Mars edges into Aries on April 9 (through May 18); inwardly, the picture you offer the world deserves a thoughtful frame. Quick-witted Mercury edges into Aries, your identity house, on April 15 (through May 3), which means minor changes to your look may build toward a striking effect. On April 17, your identity sector holds the New Moon; in practice, people may read your mood more easily than they used to. Once the life-giving Sun edges into Taurus, your money domain, on April 20 (through May 21), your income picture may sharpen after an honest look at the numbers. In your conversation sector, Venus glides into Gemini on April 24 (through May 19); people close by can prove a welcome source of news and favors. Could this be the month a quiet dream starts or grows?
column.description: The full column for this period, ready to run as one piece, its paragraphs, where it has more than one, separated by a blank line. Names the events driving it and the dates they fall on, read into the whole-sign houses of this sign. Typically 180 to 250 words. The six section fields each open on an event or standing planet of their own read through their life area, the one named in focus on the lead of this column, so render either shape and never both. Deterministic: the same sign and period always returns the same column.

focus.description: The topic this reading is mainly about: love, career, finance or health when the lead event falls in that life area, overview for a bigger-picture period. A machine value, canonical English in every language, so a client can route its own content on it (a related article, a product, a call to action) without parsing the prose; the topic field it names reads the same lead the column opens on.

type.description: Kind of event. aspect is an exact angle between two moving bodies, sign-ingress a body entering a new sign, retrograde-station a body turning retrograde or direct, lunar-phase one of the four quarters, eclipse a solar or lunar eclipse, and solar-season the Sun entering a sign.

at.description: Exact instant the event perfects, ISO 8601 to the second, on the clock the reading is read on: UTC with Z by default, the offset of timezone when one is passed on a daily, weekly or monthly reading (2026-11-13T19:27:27-05:00 in New York), the same instant either way; a yearly reading is written in UTC. Verifiable against NASA JPL Horizons for a position event and against the US Naval Observatory for a lunar phase or eclipse.

bodies.description: Bodies involved, canonical English regardless of the requested language so the value stays safe to switch on. Two entries for an aspect, faster body first. One entry for an ingress, a station, a lunar phase, or an eclipse.

name.description: Body name, canonical English in every language. Matches the entry at the same index in bodies.

sign.description: Sign this body occupies at the event timestamp, lowercase and never translated. For a sign change, the sign entered.

house.description: Whole-sign house this body occupies at the event instant, counted from the queried sign, 1 to 12.

placements.description: Each participant at the enclosing event timestamp, in bodies order: two entries for an aspect and one for every other event. Names and signs stay canonical English in every language. Each entry carries its own whole-sign house, including the second body of an aspect. Event placements can differ from positions, which reports noon on the first day of the period.

aspect.description: Angle formed, on aspect events only: conjunction, sextile, square, trine, opposition, semi-sextile, quincunx, semi-square, or sesquiquadrate.

phase.description: Exact quarter phase, on lunar-phase events only: new-moon, first-quarter, full-moon, or last-quarter. Canonical English in every language. Use to identify the phase at the event instant.

kind.description: Eclipse classification at peak, on eclipse events only: penumbral, partial, annular, or total. Canonical English in every language. Sun in bodies identifies a solar eclipse and Moon a lunar eclipse.

direction.description: Direction the body turns at the event instant, on retrograde-station events only: retrograde starts backward motion and direct ends it. Canonical English in every language. Present even when the other end of the retrograde span cannot be dated.

sign.description: Sign the event falls in, lowercase, where it has exactly one. Absent for an aspect whose two bodies stand in different signs.

house.description: Whole-sign house the event falls in, counted from the queried sign, 1 to 12. This is what turns one global sky event into a statement about this reader.

through.description: End of the window this event holds open, on the same clock as at, given only where a bounded window is a real fact about it: the orb span of an aspect, the sign span of an ingress or a season, the retrograde span of a station. Absent for a lunar phase or an eclipse, which are instants and not spans.

events.description: The dated astronomical events this reading is built on, earliest first. Every field in every row can be checked against an independent authority, so a column can be fact-checked before it is published. Empty on a period in which nothing exact happens, where the reading falls back to the standing positions instead.

name.description: Body, canonical English regardless of the requested language: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune or Pluto, in that order, one row each. Same key and values as planets[].name on the natal chart.

sign.description: Sign the body stands in at noon on the first day of the period on the reader clock, lowercase like events[].sign, never translated.

house.description: Whole-sign house that sign is for the queried sign, 1 to 12, counted as events[].house is.

isRetrograde.description: Whether the body moves retrograde at that noon. Same key as planets[].isRetrograde on the natal chart; the daily activeTransits prints the same flag as a translated string.

dignity.description: Essential dignity of the body in that sign, the same value planets[].dignity reports on the natal chart: domicile, exaltation, detriment, fall, or peregrine. Always English. A column or card that calls a body at home or exalted is backed by this value.

enteredAt.description: Instant the body entered this sign, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at. Where the entry is also a row of events[] in this response it is that row at, byte for byte. Absent only where the entry lies too far back to date.

leavesAt.description: Instant the body next leaves this sign, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at: the date a column prints in until April 15. Where it is also in events[] (the ingress that ends the stay, or the through of the ingress that began it) it is that string, byte for byte. Absent only where the exit lies too far ahead to date.

turnsDirectAt.description: Instant the body next turns direct, to the second, on the same clock as events[].at, present only while isRetrograde is true: the date a retrograde is dated by in the prose. Where the station is also in events[] it is that row at or through, byte for byte. Absent only where the turn lies too far ahead to date.

positions.description: Where each of the ten bodies stands for this reading, one row per body, so every standing claim in the prose (a body in a house, until a date, retrograde until it turns direct, exalted or at home) can be checked against the response itself. It carries state only: every aspect, lunation, eclipse, ingress or station of the period is a row of events[]. Against events[], it adds the bodies that do nothing exact in the period (events[] names only what happens), the entry and exit of the sign each stands in (events[].through carries an exit only for an ingress inside the period), the instant a retrograde body turns direct, and dignity. Against activeTransits, which the daily prints as translated strings for the seven visible bodies, it adds Uranus, Neptune and Pluto, the lowercase sign and numeric house as values, the retrograde flag as a boolean, and the three instants. Where an instant appears in both keys it is the same string. Never translated.

week.description: Position of the week inside the month, 1 first. The rows are calendar weeks, Monday to Sunday, clipped to the month at each end, so a month carries four, five or six of them. Row N is therefore the same week the weekly forecast covers, which is what lets a monthly page link straight into it.

focus.description: The life area the week turns on, in the requested language: the theme of the whole-sign house holding the strongest event the reading names inside that week, or of the strongest standing placement where the week holds no dated event. Same values as the life areas of the yearly key periods.

advice.example: Meet whoever you clash with halfway, and say plainly where you're willing to give ground.
advice.description: One practical sentence for that life area, in the requested language. No two weeks of one month repeat a sentence.

example.advice: Meet whoever you clash with halfway, and say plainly where you're willing to give ground.
Try the look you've been putting off, and choose what you want instead of what's safe.
Check how you reply when someone asks what you'd like, and try giving the honest version.
Stand by the window with your coffee and decide what you'd do if nobody needed you.
Air out the bedroom, change the sheets and make where you sleep feel looked after.

weekByWeek.description: The month read one calendar week at a time, off the same ranked events as column and events[]: the life area each week turns on, and the one thing that area asks for. Two weeks may land in the same area, because two events of a month often do; the sentence beside it is always different. Use it for the week strip of a monthly page.

date.description: Date of the event (YYYY-MM-DD) on the clock the month is read on, the day the column names it: a station at 00:27 UTC is the previous day in New York. The exact instant, to the second, is on the matching row of events[].

event.example: Full Moon in Libra, your zone of partnership.
event.description: The event in the requested language, with the sign it falls in and the life area of the whole-sign house that sign is for this zodiac sign, as a dated calendar list prints it.

Last Quarter Moon in Capricorn, your realm of career and public standing.

keyDates.description: The dates to circle this month, earliest first: every lunation and eclipse of the month, plus the headline movements the reading is built on, which are the sign changes of the slower planets and every station with the direction it turns. Each is placed in the whole-sign house it reaches for this sign. Every row is an instant the ephemeris gives, checkable against NASA JPL Horizons or the US Naval Observatory, and every row is also a row of events[], so the list cannot contradict the reading beside it.

luckyNumbers.description: Four lucky numbers for the month, each 1 to 9 and all distinct, from the traditional planetary number correspondence applied to the four planets that govern this sign this month.

luckyColor.description: Lucky color for the month, the color traditionally ruled by the planet that governs this sign this month: Sun gold, Moon silver, Mercury light blue, Venus green, Mars red, Jupiter purple, Saturn brown. When Uranus, Neptune or Pluto governs, the next most governing of the seven classical planets gives the color. Translated with the lang parameter.

compatibleSigns.description: Three zodiac signs most in tune with this sign this month, best first. Read from the real sky of the period, so the list moves with the transits instead of repeating a fixed table, and every pick can be traced in positions[]. On a quiet sky it settles on the classic element partners. For the fixed sign-to-sign pairing, read compatibleSigns from the signs endpoint.

get.description: Get the year ahead for any zodiac sign, as a long-form column plus the structured arrays a year-ahead page is built from: the slow-body themes that set the backdrop, a dated key period for each of the twelve houses, the best month for love, career, health and finance, and every eclipse and every retrograde and direct station with the house it falls in for this sign. Love, career, health, finance and advice cover the whole year, and the dated events and standing planet positions behind the copy come back beside it so an editor can check the piece before it runs. Omit the year for the one in progress, or pass any year from 1900 to 2100 to build an archive or a forecast ahead of time. Composed in 8 languages (en, tr, de, es, hi, pt, fr, ru); zh-Hans and zh-Hant read English. Yearly horoscope API, year ahead astrology, annual zodiac forecast, eclipse and retrograde calendar.

parameters.description: Response language (BCP 47). Supported: en, tr, de, es, hi, pt, fr, ru, zh-Hans, zh-Hant. Defaults to en. Coverage varies by domain, and a field with no translation in the requested language returns English.

schema.description: Selects which year counts as current when year is omitted. Defaults to UTC, so the forecast rolls over at 00:00 UTC on January 1. Your conversation realm is where inventive Uranus moves into Gemini on April 26, which suggests someone nearby might share a tip that saves you effort. On June 30, generous Jupiter arrives in Leo, your romance domain; a creative idea kept in a drawer could finally see daylight. Gracious Venus in your intimacy house shifts into retrograde October 3; what two people share may feel lighter once both feel heard. Whenever you are sizing up a bigger step before the year closes, you could take it with confidence. Diligent effort repeated every month outlasts each sudden burst.

A planetary return occurs when a transiting planet conjuncts its natal longitude, marking the beginning of a new cycle. Saturn return (~29 years) is the most significant life milestone in Western astrology. Jupiter return (~12 years) signals expansion and growth phases. Mars return (~2 years) resets energy and drive. Returns full tropical zodiac chart with all planetary positions, house cusps, and aspects. Planetary return chart API, Saturn return calculator, Jupiter return chart, Mars return forecast.

True is the osculating node and the default, because it is what most Western chart software reports; mean is the smoothed node preferred by several evolutionary schools, so pass "mean" to match one. nodeType.description: Lunar node convention. "mean" is the smoothed average node, which always moves retrograde; "true" is the osculating node, which tracks the real perturbed node, oscillates up to about 1.5 degrees either side of the mean on a 173-day cycle, and can briefly turn direct. Neither is more correct and they almost always fall in the same sign. Applies to the North and South Node. True is the osculating node and the default, because it is what most Western chart software reports; mean is the smoothed node preferred by several evolutionary schools, so pass "mean" to match one. Nothing else in the chart changes, and the two agree on the sign except when the node sits within about 1.8 degrees of a cusp. Defaults to "true".
